arxiv-2104-03832.title: Strongly CS-Rickart and dual strongly CS-Rickart objects in abelian categories
arxiv-2104-03832.creator: Septimiu Crivei, Simona Maria Radu
arxiv-2104-03832.description: Abstract . We introduce (dual) strongly relative CS-Rickart objects in abelian categories, as common generalizations of (dual) strongly relative Rickart objects and strongly extending (lifting) objects. We give general properties, and we study direct summands, (co)products of (dual) strongly relative CS-Rickart objects and classes all of whose objects are (dual) strongly self-CS-Rickart. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 18E10, 18E15, 16D90 1.

arxiv-2109-07316.title: Reinshard: An optimally sharded dual-blockchain for concurrency resolution
arxiv-2109-07316.creator: Vishal Sharma, Zengpeng Li, Pawel Szalachowski, Teik Guan Tan, Jianying Zhou
arxiv-2109-07316.description: Abstract Decentralized control, low-complexity, flexible and efficient communications are the requirements of an architecture that aims to scale blockchains beyond the current state. Such properties are attainable by reducing ledger size and providing parallel operations in the blockchain. Sharding is one of the approaches that lower the burden of the nodes and enhance performance.

arxiv-2212-01555.title: Contrastive Domain Adaptation for Time-Series via Temporal Mixup
arxiv-2212-01555.creator: Emadeldeen Eldele, Mohamed Ragab, Zhenghua Chen, Min Wu, Chee-Keong Kwoh, Xiaoli Li
arxiv-2212-01555.description: Abstract Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) has emerged as a powerful solution for the domain shift problem via transferring the knowledge from a labeled source domain to a shifted unlabeled target domain. Despite the prevalence of UDA for visual applications, it remains relatively less explored for time-series applications.

arxiv-2303-18200.title: PADME-SoSci: A Platform for Analytics and Distributed Machine Learning for the Social Sciences
arxiv-2303-18200.creator: Zeyd Boukhers 1,2 Arnim Bleier 3 Yeliz Ucer Yediel 1,5 Mio Hienstorfer-Heitmann 3 Mehrshad Jaberansary 2,4 Adamantios Koumpis 2,4 Oya Beyan 1,2,4
arxiv-2303-18200.description: Abstract . Data privacy and ownership are significant in social data science, raising legal and ethical concerns. Sharing and analyzing data is difficult when different parties own different parts of it. An approach to this challenge is to apply de-identification or anonymization techniques to the data before collecting it for analysis.

arxiv-2306-16526.title: Shilling Black-box Review-based Recommender Systems through Fake Review Generation Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 6–10, 2023; Long Beach, CA, USA Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mi
arxiv-2306-16526.creator: Hung-Yun Chiang, Yi-Syuan Chen, Yun-Zhu Song, Hong-Han Shuai, Jason S. Chang
arxiv-2306-16526.description: Abstract . Review-Based Recommender Systems (RBRS) have attracted increasing research interest due to their ability to alleviate well-known cold-start problems. RBRS utilizes reviews to construct the user and items representations. However, in this paper, we argue that such a reliance on reviews may instead expose systems to the risk of being shilled.

arxiv-2307-09901.title: Using Circulation to Mitigate Spurious Equilibria in Control Barrier Function
arxiv-2307-09901.creator: Vinicius Mariano Gonçalves, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Anthony Tzes, Farshad Khorrami
arxiv-2307-09901.description: Abstract Control Barrier Functions and Quadratic Programming are increasingly used for designing controllers that consider critical safety constraints. However, like Artificial Potential Fields, they can suffer from the stable spurious equilibrium point problem, which can result in the controller failing to reach the goal. To address this issue, we propose introducing circulation inequalities as a constraint.

arxiv-2311-00091.title: The derivation problem for one type of bimodules over group algebras

arxiv-2311-00091.description: Abstract The derivation problem is a familiar one concerning group algebras, particularly L 1 ​ ( G ) L_{1}(G) and von Neumann algebras. In this paper, we study the Banach bimodule ℓ p ​ ( G ) \ell_{p}(G) , which is generated by the ℓ p \ell_{p} norm over a specific class of groups with well-organized conjugacy classes.

arxiv-2402-10541.title: Cousin complexes in motivic homotopy theory
arxiv-2402-10541.creator: Andrei Druzhinin, Håkon Kolderup, Paul Arne Østvær
arxiv-2402-10541.description: Abstract . We investigate Cousin (bi-)complexes in the setting of motives. For essentially smooth local schemes, the columns of the Cousin bicomplex with coefficients in any stable motivic homotopy type is shown to be acyclic. On the other hand, we also construct a family of non-acyclic Cousin complexes over any positive dimensional base scheme.

arxiv-2505-09660.title: On Measuring Intrinsic Causal Attributions in Deep Neural Networks Saptarshi was a Fulbright-Nehru Doctoral Research Fellow at the University at Buffalo during this work.
arxiv-2505-09660.creator: Saptarshi Saha, Dhruv Vansraj Rathore, Soumadeep Saha, Utpal Garain, David Doermann
arxiv-2505-09660.description: Abstract Quantifying the causal influence of input features within neural networks has become a topic of increasing interest. Existing approaches typically assess direct, indirect, and total causal effects. This work treats NNs as structural causal models (SCMs) and extends our focus to include intrinsic causal contributions (ICC). We propose an identifiable generative post-hoc framework for quantifying ICC.

arxiv-2508-17583.title: On the analysis of eruptive events with non-radial evolution
arxiv-2508-17583.creator: Abril Sahade, M. Valeria Sieyra, Mariana Cécere
arxiv-2508-17583.description: Abstract Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are major drivers of space weather disturbances, and their deflection from the radial direction critically affects their potential impact on Earth. While the influence of the surrounding magnetic field in guiding CME trajectories is well established, accurately predicting non-radial propagation remains a challenge.

pmc-12713211.title: AI-based pathomics in kidney diseases: progress and application

pmc-12713211.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025).
